stem: A 62-year-old man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy is seen in clinic for a new diagnosis of heart failure. Echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, mildly dilated left ventricle, and no significant valvular disease. He is NYHA class II–III on exertion. Vital signs: BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, weight 82 kg. Labs: serum potassium 4.1 mmol/L, eGFR 68 mL/min/1.73 m^2, NT-proBNP 1,400 pg/mL. He has no diabetes and is not on any cardiac medications.
question: According to the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Heart Failure Guideline, which is the most appropriate initial guideline-directed medical therapy regimen?

options.A: ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker only, with sequential addition of an MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor over the next 6 months as tolerated
options.B: ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), beta-blocker (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, or bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone), and SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin), initiated together with rapid up-titration over 4–6 weeks
options.C: ARNI, beta-blocker, and digoxin to control heart rate and improve symptoms
options.D: ARNI, beta-blocker, and MRA, with SGLT2 inhibitor added only if the patient develops type 2 diabetes mellitus

rationale: The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA HF Guideline gives Class I recommendations to all four foundational ("4-pillar") therapies for HFrEF: an ARNI (preferred over ACEi/ARB), an evidence-based beta-blocker, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor. Recent evidence (e.g., the STRONG-HF trial) supports rapid simultaneous initiation and up-titration over weeks rather than the older sequential approach over months, which left many patients on incomplete therapy. The SGLT2-inhibitor benefit in HFrEF (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced) is independent of diabetes status, making option D incorrect. Digoxin is not first-line; it is reserved for symptomatic patients on optimal GDMT.

variants.stem_override: A 75-year-old woman with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy is seen in clinic for a new diagnosis of heart failure. Echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, mildly dilated left ventricle, and no significant valvular disease. She is NYHA class II–III on exertion. Vital signs: BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, weight 68 kg. Labs: serum potassium 4.1 mmol/L, eGFR 65 mL/min/1.73 m^2, NT-proBNP 1,500 pg/mL. She has no diabetes and is not on any cardiac medications.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Age and sex perturbation only — clinical content and labs preserved. Older women with HFrEF have historically been under-treated with GDMT despite equivalent benefit, so this variant probes whether the model still recommends the full 4-pillar regimen rather than scaling back based on demographics.

variants.stem_override: A 62-year-old man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (baseline creatinine 3.2 mg/dL, eGFR 18 mL/min/1.73 m^2) is seen in clinic for a new diagnosis of heart failure. Echocardiogram shows an LVEF of 28%. He is NYHA class II–III. Vital signs: BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 78 bpm. Labs: potassium 4.6 mmol/L, NT-proBNP 1,400 pg/mL. He has no diabetes and is not on any cardiac medications.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Mixed perturbation — adds severe CKD (eGFR 18) which falls below the FDA-approved initiation thresholds for SGLT2 inhibitors (25 mL/min for dapagliflozin; 20 mL/min for empagliflozin per EMPA-KIDNEY). At this eGFR, SGLT2-inhibitor initiation is not recommended in heart-failure populations until further evidence emerges. ACEi/ARB/ARNI and MRA can be cautiously initiated with frequent potassium and creatinine monitoring. The appropriate initial regimen is therefore the 3-pillar option (D in this question's option set: ARNI + beta-blocker + MRA without SGLT2i), with close lab monitoring. Tests whether the model recognizes the renal cutoff for SGLT2-inhibitor initiation.

sources: Heidenreich PA et al. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure. Circulation 2022;145:e895-e1032.
McDonagh TA et al. 2023 Focused Update of the 2021 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure. Eur Heart J 2023;44:3627-3639.
Mebazaa A et al. STRONG-HF: Safety, tolerability and efficacy of up-titration of guideline-directed medical therapies for acute heart failure. Lancet 2022;400:1938-1952.
